boundary.purpose: Exact neutral implementation handoff for result-document ownership, dataset data integrity, all canonical viewer types and quick projections, data interchange, precision, persistence, migration, recovery, publication, and platform composition.
boundary.singlePersistenceAuthority: The canonical result-document object is the only persistent results presentation model. Viewer document types are typed panes within it and quick modes are routing projections only.
boundary.sourceDataAuthority: Immutable datasets own source samples, event streams, axes, family coordinates, run manifests, integrity, and provenance. Result documents own versioned presentation and declared derived artifacts only.
boundary.prohibitedSilentBehavior: Alignment, interpolation, resampling, unit conversion, type conversion, numeric rounding, truncation, aggregation, decimation, missing-value replacement, and provenance rebinding are never silent.
boundary.readiness: This design contract and its generated coverage do not prove implementation, numeric correctness, engine support, decoder or encoder availability, platform qualification, accessibility conformance, release readiness, or sign-off eligibility.

authority.changeOwner: results data lifecycle and results workspace

crossContractReferences.use: Virtualization, progressive rendering, exact-versus-reduced data, cancellation, backpressure, pressure, cache, renderer recovery, and evidence budgets are referenced here and not redefined.
Current desktop, browser, and tablet result-authoring modes and platform capability dimensions are projected from this authority; phone/mobile remains an explicit unavailable future-platform record.
Structured engineering alternatives, keyboard operation, annotations, localization, and accessibility qualification remain owned by this authority.
Viewer components, visual states, chart presentation, print styling, motion, contrast, and visual qualification remain owned by the design system.

graph.datasetBindings: References immutable dataset identities, digests, scopes, protection, and currentness without embedding a second mutable source model.
graph.panes: Ordered typed viewer instances with layout and shared-domain relationships.
graph.entities: Stable pane, trace, family, axis, unit, cursor, linked-probe, marker, measurement, calculator-expression, and annotation identities.

persistentModel.revisionSemantics: Every committed authoring transaction creates one new document revision by semantic delta; autosave, undo, redo, merge, import, migration, and recovery never rewrite an existing durable revision.

quickModePolicy.rule: A quick mode resolves to one canonical viewer document type and persists only through its owning result-document pane and entity graph.

forbidden: canvas-only state without a structural representation

datasetContract.ownership: Immutable dataset and results data lifecycle

integrity.policy: Numeric access requires verified structural and content integrity for the exact requested scope; cached or partial verification cannot imply complete verification.
integrity.chunks: Chunk digests, ordering, logical coordinates, compression and encoding versions, and aggregate root digest are retained.
integrity.signatures: Signatures bind the manifest and root digest; signature trust and byte integrity are reported separately.

provenance.graph: Every source or derived value resolves through stable dataset, run, job, plan, input, model, engine, platform, algorithm, and actor identities.
derivationReceiptFields: operation and algorithm IDs and versions
provenance.missingPolicy: Missing provenance blocks promotion to verification or release evidence and is never replaced by UI labels or filenames.

currentness.comparisonBasis: Currentness compares stable input, plan, model, engine, platform, mapping, and derivation identities rather than modification time alone.
currentness.propagation: A changed dependency marks dependent traces, expressions, measurements, comparisons, reports, and evidence stale while preserving the historical revision.

protectedData.enforcement: Authorize every operation at its exact data and destination scope; document access never implies export, print, share, or decrypt authority.
protectedData.redaction: Redaction creates a new derived artifact with policy, removed fields, aggregation or masking methods, source digests, and irreversible disclosure review.
protectedData.secrets: Credentials, tokens, encryption keys, and protected raw payloads never enter document presentation state, logs, telemetry, or clipboard without explicit authority.

datasetContract.sourceMutation: Result authoring, comparison, visualization, report, export, migration, and recovery never mutate an immutable dataset.

formatContract.overwritePolicy: Never overwrite a valid destination before a complete staged artifact verifies. Existing artifacts are versioned, atomically replaced with recoverable prior bytes, or left unchanged.
formatContract.unsupportedPolicy: Unknown formats, versions, dialects, encodings, or semantic mappings are unavailable-with-reason and never guessed.

precisionContract.sourceAuthority: The stored dataset type, lexical source when applicable, byte order, scale, unit, missing-value representation, and numeric contract are authoritative.

binaryFloatingPoint.defaultText: Shortest correctly rounded round-trip representation; fixed digit limits are never inferred from the display.
fullPrecisionOptions: raw encoded bits with type and byte order
binaryFloatingPoint.f32Guidance: At least 9 significant decimal digits when a fixed round-trip form is explicitly required.
binaryFloatingPoint.f64Guidance: At least 17 significant decimal digits when a fixed round-trip form is explicitly required.

precisionContract.complex: Preserve real and imaginary components as the source authority. RI, magnitude/angle, and dB/angle are explicit representations with angle unit, branch, zero behavior, reference, and precision.
precisionContract.integerRationalDecimal: Preserve width, signedness, exact integer ticks, numerator and denominator, decimal scale, and lexical precision as applicable.
precisionContract.timeAndFrequency: Preserve integer ticks or exact rational scale and epoch. Floating display units never replace the exact time or frequency coordinate.
precisionContract.specialValues: NaN payload disposition, positive and negative infinity, signed zero, missing, unknown, high impedance, invalid, and overflow states remain distinct and schema-declared.
precisionContract.unitConversion: Only dimension-compatible, versioned, reviewed conversions may be applied. Scale, offset, constants, uncertainty, source and destination units, and rounding remain in the receipt.
precisionContract.rounding: Round-to-nearest ties-to-even is permitted only when an explicitly selected target representation requires rounding and the receipt records it; other modes require explicit selection. Silent rounding, truncation, saturation, clamping, flush-to-zero, and locale-dependent parsing are prohibited.
prohibited: precision claims based on viewport pixels

persistenceContract.commit: Write a new revision to staging, validate closed schema, references, integrity, authority, quota, and reopen behavior, durably flush required metadata and payload, then atomically publish the revision pointer.
persistenceContract.autosave: Autosave writes owner-scoped recoverable draft revisions with base identity and never becomes a hidden parallel result model.
persistenceContract.conflict: Optimistic base-revision checks retain both semantic deltas; merge, fork, supersede, or cancel is explicit and last-writer-wins is forbidden.

migration.strategy: Copy-on-write inspect, plan, backup, migrate, validate, reopen, compare semantic identity, commit new revision, retain lineage; never destructively rewrite the only copy.

migration.olderUnknown: Block write and require a registered migration; safe metadata inspection and byte-preserving export may remain available.
migration.newer: Open safe metadata or compatibility view read-only; never down-convert or overwrite silently.

recovery.evaluation: Verify identity, schema, payload and binding digests, provenance, protection, completeness, compatibility, and expected semantic delta before selection.
recovery.originalPolicy: Preserve original bytes and diagnostics until a reviewed retention policy permits disposal.
recovery.commit: Recovery creates a new revision with candidate and predecessor identities; recovered never means source integrity was retroactively valid.

persistenceContract.quickModeRule: Quick modes have no file, table, keyspace, revision, autosave, journal, migration, recovery, or conflict owner separate from the result-document.

failureCodes.trigger: The document envelope, entity graph, type ID, or required field fails schema validation.
failureCodes.effect: Block commit and retain the last valid revision.
failureCodes.recovery: Focus the exact invalid paths and allow repair, safe source return, or import cancellation.

failureCodes.trigger: A stable dataset binding cannot resolve.
failureCodes.effect: Open the document with an unresolved binding state and no fabricated data.
failureCodes.recovery: Locate an exact digest match, request access, rebind through reviewed impact, or return to source.

failureCodes.trigger: Required digests or signatures have not completed verification.
failureCodes.effect: Permit metadata inspection only and block numeric trust, export, comparison, and evidence use.
failureCodes.recovery: Complete verification or cancel without changing the source.

failureCodes.trigger: Bytes do not match the bound content digest.
failureCodes.effect: Quarantine the candidate and preserve the expected identity and received bytes separately.
failureCodes.recovery: Locate a verified replica, invoke recovery, or retain a diagnostic bundle.

failureCodes.trigger: Storage, decoding, chunk, checksum, or structural validation proves corruption.
failureCodes.effect: Mark the dataset corrupted and prevent silent fallback to partial or cached values.
failureCodes.recovery: Evaluate verified recovery candidates while preserving original evidence.

failureCodes.trigger: Only a declared subset of expected samples, families, chunks, or event ranges is present.
failureCodes.effect: Expose exact present and missing scope and block claims requiring completeness.
failureCodes.recovery: Resume acquisition or transfer, use an explicitly partial workflow, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: Input, model, plan, run, or mapping revision no longer matches the bound provenance.
failureCodes.effect: Preserve historical review while marking dependent traces, measurements, comparisons, and reports stale.
failureCodes.recovery: Open the current source, rerun, rebind as a new revision, or retain the historical document.

failureCodes.trigger: Identity lacks read, derive, copy, export, print, share, or decrypt authority.
failureCodes.effect: Deny only the unauthorized operation, preserve safe metadata where policy permits, and disclose the exact authority.
failureCodes.recovery: Request authority, select an allowed redacted scope, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: A viewer family, external capability, decoder, encoder, or operation is not entitled.
failureCodes.effect: Preserve project and document identities and show unavailable-with-reason.
failureCodes.recovery: Acquire entitlement, use an exact supported alternative, hand off when optional, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: The selected format or version has no declared adapter.
failureCodes.effect: Do not guess a dialect or parse as a similar format.
failureCodes.recovery: Choose a declared adapter, install a governed connector, preserve the source, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: Dialect, delimiter, locale, encoding, axis, complex representation, unit, or shape is ambiguous.
failureCodes.effect: Block import or export preview from committing.
failureCodes.recovery: Require exact options and show a deterministic preview before retry.

failureCodes.trigger: Input violates the selected format grammar or typed mapping.
failureCodes.effect: Retain the staged source and report bounded exact locations without partial commit.
failureCodes.recovery: Repair mapping or source, select a correct dialect, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: A conversion, formatter, target type, digit limit, or range cannot preserve required values.
failureCodes.effect: Block commit and identify every affected column, trace, array, or value class.
failureCodes.recovery: Choose a lossless target or create a reviewed derived artifact with method and error bounds.

failureCodes.trigger: A target representation would overflow, underflow, saturate, flush, or lose a special value.
failureCodes.effect: Block by default; never clamp, saturate, flush, or replace silently.
failureCodes.recovery: Select a wider representation or explicitly reviewed derived conversion.

failureCodes.trigger: Quantities have incompatible dimension vectors or an undefined conversion.
failureCodes.effect: Block shared axis, arithmetic, comparison, or merge.
failureCodes.recovery: Choose compatible quantities or define and review a versioned conversion as a derived artifact.

failureCodes.trigger: Compared domains do not share exact coordinate identity.
failureCodes.effect: Show unaligned sources separately and block difference or regression claims.
failureCodes.recovery: Select and review a named alignment method or restrict to exact matching coordinates.

failureCodes.trigger: A requested value or comparison has no exact stored coordinate.
failureCodes.effect: Return no exact value and identify the gap.
failureCodes.recovery: Navigate to a stored sample or explicitly select and record an interpolation method.

failureCodes.trigger: Source grids differ and the requested operation requires a common grid.
failureCodes.effect: Block combined arithmetic and do not treat display pixels as samples.
failureCodes.recovery: Select a reviewed grid, method, boundary rule, anti-alias policy, and error disposition.

failureCodes.trigger: Comparison inputs, methods, units, alignment, interpolation, or resampling receipts are incomplete.
failureCodes.effect: Mark comparison unresolved and exclude it from verification or release evidence.
failureCodes.recovery: Complete the missing declarations or cancel the comparison.

failureCodes.trigger: No registered migration path exists from the stored schema version.
failureCodes.effect: Preserve bytes and open safe metadata or read-only compatibility only.
failureCodes.recovery: Install a reviewed migrator, export with the originating version, or fork a recovery copy.

failureCodes.trigger: The document schema is newer than the reader.
failureCodes.effect: Never down-convert or overwrite; expose safe metadata and protected export only.
failureCodes.recovery: Open with a compatible version or save a separately named reviewed conversion.

failureCodes.trigger: The durable base revision changed before commit.
failureCodes.effect: Keep both revisions and block last-writer-wins replacement.
failureCodes.recovery: Compare semantic deltas, merge explicitly, fork, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: Staging, cache, journal, export, report, or commit lacks durable capacity.
failureCodes.effect: Stop before corrupting the prior revision and distinguish reconstructable cache from durable data.
failureCodes.recovery: Free allowed cache, select another destination, resume from receipt, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: The user or owner requests cancellation.
failureCodes.effect: Stop admitting work, retain complete atomic units and receipt, and label all partial artifacts.
failureCodes.recovery: Return, discard staged partials, or resume only when the operation declares it safe.

failureCodes.trigger: GPU, canvas, WebGL, WebGPU, native renderer, or device context is unavailable or lost.
failureCodes.effect: Preserve document state and exact structured alternatives; never mark data failed solely because a renderer failed.
failureCodes.recovery: Recover renderer, select a qualified fallback, continue structured review, or cancel visual refinement.

failureCodes.trigger: Encoding, writing, signing, transfer, or final integrity verification does not complete.
failureCodes.effect: Do not publish the destination as successful and retain the prior destination.
failureCodes.recovery: Resume through receipt, retry to a new staged destination, or retain diagnostics.

failureCodes.trigger: Platform printing, page renderer, font, color profile, protected-data authority, or destination is unavailable.
failureCodes.effect: Preserve the report and show unavailable-with-reason without substituting a screenshot.
failureCodes.recovery: Resolve the dependency, export an exact declared publication format, or cancel.

failureCodes.trigger: A recovery candidate fails digest, schema, provenance, compatibility, or completeness validation.
failureCodes.effect: Keep the candidate quarantined and preserve the original.
failureCodes.recovery: Try another verified candidate or escalate with a retained diagnostic bundle.
